distractors.reason: 'Count in' means include someone in a plan (Count me in!), not trust a person.
We don't say 'count at' to mean trust someone; 'at' is used with places, times and targets.
'Count for' means 'be important or valuable' (Every vote counts for something). It does not mean trust.

example_sentence: My best friend is very reliable, so I can always count ___ her.
l1_interference: Uwaga: po polsku mówimy 'liczyć na kogoś', więc przyimek 'on' jest naturalny, ale nie tłumacz 'liczyć z kimś' jako 'count with' ani 'liczyć do' jako 'count to' – te konstrukcje w angielskim znaczą co innego lub są błędne.
explanation: 'Count on' means trust someone to help you or to be there when you need them. It is a common phrasal verb used with people.

related_collocations.example: You can rely on my brother to keep a secret.
Our plan depends on the weather.

memory_tip: COUNT ON = trust someone (count on a friend) | COUNT IN = include someone (count me in)
